extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NIA/NIH grant applicants (F99/K00, K99/R00), early-stage investigators, mentors and research administrators preparing fellowship/career-development applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and example materials for preparing and revising NIA/NIH fellowship and early-career (F99/K00, K99/R00) applications, using sample initial submissions, resubmissions, full applications, and summary statements to inform applicants' writing and revision strategy. Emphasizes following current FOA formatting rules and tailoring applications to individual research and career plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples are examples, not templates
rubrics_metrics.description: These are only examples of successful applications and are not meant to be a template for future applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not copy sample text or structure verbatim; instead use samples to learn approaches to organization, level of detail, and grantsmanship. Tailor content to your own project and career-development plan; seek individual advice from mentors and peers when preparing your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor application to your specific research and career development plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure that your application is tailored to your specific research and career development plan and seek individual advice from mentors and peers as you prepare your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize aims, training plans, career development statements, and mentorship descriptions to reflect your unique background and goals. Use mentors/peers to evaluate whether the application convincingly links training activities to career objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always follow the funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting, page limits, required documents, and forms may vary by FOA and by NIH/NIH component; ensure you use the current forms and instructions for the specific announcement. Even if samples show good grantsmanship, they may not conform to the latest FOA-specific formatting or submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware sample applications may be outdated
rubrics_metrics.description: Although these applications demonstrate good grantsmanship, time has passed since these grantees applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify current application forms, policy updates, and FOA changes before relying on sample content or structure. Treat examples as historical illustrations rather than authoritative current templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted use of sample materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The awardee allows you to use the material (e.g., data, writing, graphics) it shared in this application only for nonprofit educational purposes provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigator, awardee organization, and NIH NIA are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not republish, modify, or use sample materials for commercial purposes; keep materials unchanged and provide proper attribution to PI/awardee organization/NIH NIA when using them for educational review or instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use paired initial and resubmission files to learn revision strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The F99/K00 and K99/R00 resources below represent the initial submissions and subsequent resubmissions of applications from applicants who received an excellent score and were funded upon resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare initial (not funded) applications and their summary statements with the funded resubmissions to identify how applicants addressed reviewer concerns, reworked aims, clarified approach, or improved career development plans. Use these comparisons to guide how you revise in response to reviewer feedback.
